title: Protocol to study the role of a human nuclear m6A RNA reader on chromatin-associated RNA targets
protocol: Lyse cells to obtain the cytoplasmic fraction and nuclei.
Isolate nuclei and lyse them sequentially to collect the nucleoplasm and chromatin-associated fractions.
Perform SDS-PAGE and Western blot analyses on an aliquot of each collected fraction.
Add TRIzol for RNA extraction from each subcellular fraction.
Maintain all steps at 4°C to minimize degradation of proteins and RNA.
Add RNase inhibitor to all buffers to prevent RNA degradation.
Harvest the transfected cells 72 hours after transfection.
Gently scrape the cells using a cell scraper and recover all cells, including floating ones.
Transfer the cell suspension to labeled 15 mL polypropylene conical tubes.
Centrifuge the suspension at 400 × g for 5 minutes.
Remove the supernatant and resuspend the pellet gently in 500 μL of cold PBS without calcium and magnesium.
Transfer the cells to labeled 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tubes.
Centrifuge the cell suspension at 400 × g for 5 minutes.
Remove the supernatant and keep the cells on ice.
Resuspend the cell pellet in 400 μL of cold fractionation lysis buffer, adding DTT and PMSF before resuspension.
Incubate the suspension for 10 minutes on ice.
Centrifuge the suspension at 4°C for 5 minutes at 400 × g.
Collect the supernatant corresponding to the cytoplasmic fraction and store it on ice.
Take a 20 μL aliquot of the supernatant for SDS-PAGE analysis.
Wash the pellet using cold fractionation washing buffer.
Gently resuspend the pellet with 200 μL of cold fractionation washing buffer by tapping the tube or using a pre-cut pipet tip.
Centrifuge at 4°C for 5 minutes at 400 × g.
Remove the supernatant to obtain a final pellet containing the washed nuclei.
Add 1 mL of TRIzol Reagent to the remaining cytoplasmic fraction (380 μL) and vortex thoroughly for 1 minute at room temperature.
Incubate the sample for 2–3 minutes at room temperature.
Flash freeze the sample in liquid nitrogen.
Resuspend the washed nuclei in 200 μL of fractionation nuclear lysis buffer.
Vortex for 30 seconds and incubate samples for 20 minutes on ice.
Centrifuge for 10 minutes at 20,000 × g at 4°C.
Collect the supernatant (corresponding to the nucleoplasm fraction) and store it on ice.
Take a 20 μL aliquot from the supernatant for SDS-PAGE analysis.
Resuspend the remaining pellet in 200 μL of fractionation nuclear lysis buffer and keep it on ice.
Take a 20 μL aliquot from this resuspended fraction for SDS-PAGE analysis.
Add 1 mL of TRIzol Reagent to the remaining nucleoplasm and chromatin-associated fractions (180 μL) and vortex thoroughly for 1 minute at room temperature.
Incubate the sample for 2–3 minutes at room temperature.
Flash freeze the samples in liquid nitrogen.
Resuspend the pellet in 200 μL of 10 mM Tris pH 7.5, 700 mM NaCl.
Vortex for 30 seconds and incubate for 20 minutes on ice.
Centrifuge for 5 minutes at 20,000 × g at 4°C.
Recover the supernatant containing the soluble chromatin-associated fraction and store it on ice.
Resuspend the nuclear insoluble fraction in 200 μL of nuclear lysis buffer and store it on ice.
Analyze the purity of subcellular fractions by SDS-PAGE and western blot analysis using specific protein markers.
Load one volume (i.e., 4 μL) of cytoplasmic fraction for SDS-PAGE and western blot analysis.
Load two volumes (i.e., 8 μL) of nuclear fractions (nucleoplasmic and chromatin associated) for SDS-PAGE and western blot analysis.
Thaw frozen samples obtained after adding TRIzol at room temperature (20°C–22°C).
Vortex samples thoroughly to homogenize.
Add 0.2 mL of chloroform and vortex for 30 seconds at room temperature (20°C–22°C).
Incubate the mixture for 5–10 minutes at room temperature (20°C–22°C).
Centrifuge the mixture at 12,000 × g for 15 minutes at 4°C.
Carefully transfer the aqueous phase to a new microcentrifuge tube without disturbing other phases.
Add 0.5 mL of isopropanol to the aqueous phase and mix by inverting the tube several times.
Incubate the mixture for 10 minutes at room temperature (20°C–22°C).
Centrifuge the mixture at 12,000 × g for 10 minutes at 4°C.
Remove the supernatant without touching the pellet.
Wash the pellet with 1 mL of cold 75% ethanol and centrifuge at 7,500 × g for 5 minutes at 4°C.
Do not resuspend the pellet when adding 75% ethanol.
Remove the supernatant after washing and allow the RNA pellet to air-dry.
Resuspend the pellet in 20 μL of RNase-free water for cytoplasmic RNAs or 10 μL for other fractions, depending on the size of the pellet.
Incubate the resuspended sample at room temperature for 10 minutes.
Determine the RNA concentration and the 260/280 O.D. ratio using a NanoDrop UV spectrophotometer.
Evaluate the RNA integrity by electrophoresis on a 1% agarose gel stained with GelGreen Nucleic Acid Stain following the manufacturer’s instructions.
Treat 2 μg of RNA with RNase-free DNase I following the mixture indicated below.
Incubate for 20 min at 37°C in a thermocycler.
Add 1.88 μL of 50 mM EDTA to the RNA-DNase mixture and incubate 10 min at 70°C in a thermocycler.
Hybridize primers to the DNase-treated RNA following the mixture indicated below for 10 min at 65°C in a thermocycler.
Place the samples on ice immediately after hybridization.
Incubate for 10 min at 25°C, 40 min at 55°C and 5 min at 85°C using a thermocycler.
Cross-link the cells with 540 μL of methanol-free formaldehyde dropwise to reach a final concentration of 1%.
Incubate the cells for 15 minutes at room temperature (20°C-22°C) under gentle agitation.
Quench the reaction by adding 1 mL of 2.5 M glycine to achieve a final glycine concentration of 125 mM.
Incubate the mixture for 5 minutes at room temperature (20°C-22°C) under agitation.
Using a cell scraper and at room temperature, collect the cells into a 50 mL centrifuge tube.
Centrifuge the cells for 3 min at 1,250 × g at 4°C.
Remove the supernatant and resuspend the pellet with 20 mL of cold PBS without calcium and magnesium.
Centrifuge the cells as described above.
Wash a second time the pellet with 10 mL of cold PBS without calcium and magnesium.
Keep the washed cells pellet on ice.
Resuspend the cell pellet in 400 μL of RIP lysis buffer and incubate 10 min on ice.
Sonicate the sample in a cold-water bath sonicator (Active motif) for 10 min with a cycle of 30 s “on”/30 s “off” at 30% amplitude.
Centrifuge the sample at 1,000 × g for 5 min at 4°C and collect the supernatant in a new labeled microcentrifuge tube.
Resuspend the remaining pellet in 400 μL of RIP lysis buffer.
Sonicate as described in step 18.b.
Centrifuge at 1,000 × g for 5 min at 4°C.
Combine the supernatant to the one collected in step 18.c.
Repeat steps 18.d and 18.e. to obtain a 1.2 mL final volume of cell lysate.
Adapt the number of sonication cycles for protein-dependent recovery of chromatin-associated SATIII RNAs associated with YTHDC1.
Incubate lysates for 1 hour at 30°C after adding DNase Buffer and DNase I.
Stop DNase reaction by adding EDTA.
Centrifuge samples for 5 minutes at 15,000 × g at 4°C.
Transfer supernatant into a new microcentrifuge tube.
Incubate DNase-treated lysates with antibody anti-human YTHDC1 or irrelevant IgG at 4°C for 1 hour.
Prepare protein A-Sepharose beads by washing three times in RIP lysis buffer and resuspending in 20% (w/v) concentration of RIP lysis buffer.
Centrifuge all samples at 500 × g during centrifugation steps.
Do not vortex the protein A-Sepharose beads.
Add 125 μL of prewashed protein A-Sepharose beads to the lysate after a 1-hour incubation.
Incubate the mixture with beads at 4°C for another hour.
Centrifuge the sample at 500 × g for 2 minutes and remove the supernatant.
Wash the beads by adding 1 mL of RIP lysis buffer.
Mix gently by inverting the tube 5 to 6 times.
Centrifuge the sample at 500 × g for 2 minutes and remove the supernatant.
Repeat washing steps using RIP lysis buffer with 500 mM NaCl and 10 U/mL RiboLock.
Wash beads by adding 1 mL of RIP wash buffer.
Mix gently by inverting the tube 5 to 6 times.
Centrifuge the sample at 500 × g for 2 minutes and remove the supernatant.
Wash the beads by adding 1 mL of TE-DTT buffer.
Mix gently by inverting the tube 5 to 6 times.
Centrifuge the sample at 500 × g for 2 minutes.
Remove the supernatant.
Add 100 μL of RIP first elution buffer and incubate at 65°C for 20 minutes.
Centrifuge the sample at 10,000 × g for 30 seconds.
Transfer the supernatant into a new microcentrifuge tube.
Add 150 μL of RIP second elution buffer onto the beads and mix well by vortexing for 10 seconds.
Centrifuge the sample at 10,000 × g for 30 seconds.
Collect the supernatant and pool it with the one collected previously.
Incubate the sample at 65°C overnight (12 hours to 16 hours) to reverse cross-link.
Optional: Incubate the sample at 67°C for 4 hours to reverse cross-link.
Add 200 μL of RIP_TE_DTT_Proteinase K buffer and incubate for 30 minutes at 65°C.
Optional: Add 200 μL of RIP_TE_DTT_Proteinase K buffer and incubate for 2 hours at 37°C or 1 hour at 42°C.
Add 55 μL of 3 M NaOAc pH 5.2 to each sample under a fume hood.
Under a fume hood, add 500 μL of Acid-Phenol:Chloroform:isoamyl alcohol pH 4.5 (125:24:1) and mix well by vortexing for 10 seconds.
Centrifuge the sample for 5 minutes at 10,000 × g room temperature (20°C to 22°C).
Collect the upper phase containing the nucleic acids into a new tube.
Under a fume hood, add 500 μL of chloroform and mix well with a 10-second vortexing.
Centrifuge the sample for 5 minutes at 10,000 × g room temperature (20°C to 22°C).
Collect the upper phase containing the nucleic acids into a new tube.
Add 1 mL of 100% ethanol and 2 μL of glycogen to precipitate nucleic acids.
Incubate the mixture at -80°C for 20 min.
Centrifuge at 4°C for 20 min at 10,000 × g.
Carefully remove the supernatant.
Wash the pellet with 1 mL of 70% ethanol.
Centrifuge at 10,000 × g for 5 min at 4°C.
Remove the supernatant after washing.
Resuspend the RNA in 20 μL of TE containing 5 mM DTT and 10 U/mL RiboLock.
Analyze purified RNAs by RT-qPCR as described in steps 15–16.
Perform immunoprecipitation with an antibody against the protein of interest (here human YTHDC1).
Perform immunoprecipitation in parallel with human irrelevant IgG as a negative control.
Extract RNA from each RIP sample.
Use primers that amplify specific targets for RT-qPCR analysis.
Use control RNA for RT-qPCR analysis.
Calculate enrichment HSP/tRNA using the 2-ΔΔCT method.
